sentences.text: Hexinlusaurus was a small, fast-moving herbivore belonging to the basal ornithischian group from the Middle Jurassic of China.
This species is distinguished by a marked concavity extending over the lateral surface of the postorbital bone, a feature not seen in other basal ornithischians.
The genus name honors Professor He Xin-Lu of Chengdu University of Technology, who first named the specimen.
Hexinlusaurus is considered a link between the Fabrosauridae and Hypsilophodontidae families.
However, its classification has varied, with it being assigned to Hypsilophodontidae by Alifanov and Saveliev in 2014 and to Neornithischia by Han et al. in 2012 and Madzia et al. in 2018.

Hexinlusaurus lived approximately 165 to 161 million years ago, from the Bathonian to Callovian stages, in what is now Asia, though some estimates suggest a range from 170.9 to 154.8 million years ago spanning the Bajocian to Oxfordian stages.
